# Collingwood Weekly
> **A forty-million-dollar ticket sold in Grey County was claimed hours before the prize expired.**

**What You Need to Know:** A forty-million-dollar ticket sold in Grey County was claimed hours before the prize expired. OLG says the ticket was validated at a lottery terminal and that rightful ownership still has to be confirmed. South Georgian Bay also has its new council slates, and Grey County's Gather in Grey campaign took a provincial tourism award.

### The Week's Stories
**$40M Lotto ticket sold in Grey County claimed hours before expiry: CKNX News Today**
A $40 million LOTTO MAX ticket sold in Grey County was validated at an OLG lottery terminal with just hours left before a midnight deadline. CKNX News Today reported that the ticket was sold for the October 28, 2025 draw. OLG said it has contacted the person or persons who validated the ticket and that the next step is a meeting to determine whether they are the rightful owners. OLG said prize claims over $1,000 are reviewed, and that a retailer sale means the corporation does not know who bought the ticket. OLG had said that if nobody came forward by the end of Wednesday, October 28, the prize would return to the Lotto Max pool and would have been Canada's second-largest unclaimed Lotto Max prize, behind a $70 million ticket from the June 28, 2022 draw sold in Scarborough. Source: [cknxnewstoday.ca](https://cknxnewstoday.ca/midwestern/news/2026/10/28/40m-lotto-ticket-sold-in-grey-county-claimed-hours-before-expiry) Source: [cknxnewstoday.ca](https://cknxnewstoday.ca/midwestern/news/2026/10/27/40m-grey-county-lotto-ticket-could-become-canadas-second-largest-unclaimed-prize)

**2026 Municipal Election Results – Collingwood, Wasaga Beach, Clearview Twp & Town of Blue Mountains: Bayshore Broadcasting News Centre**
Bayshore Broadcasting listed the south Georgian Bay results. In Collingwood, Yvonne Hamlin is mayor and Chris Potts is deputy mayor, with councillors Christopher Baines, Marianne Mcleod, Rob Ring, Ian MacCulloch, Jan Ferrigan, James McCrimmon and Steve Perry; CollingwoodToday reported Hamlin was re-elected. In Wasaga Beach, CTV News reported the results were heavily delayed and that Brian Smith will return as mayor; Bayshore listed Mike Foley as deputy mayor and Joe Belanger, Sasha-Rose Dileo, Kyle Graves, Ellen Timms and Richard White as councillors. In Clearview, Bayshore listed Robert Macarthur as mayor, Justin McGillvray as deputy mayor, and ward councillors Craig Houghton, Gary Walters, John Broderick, Ken Walker and Rachel Brooks; CollingwoodToday reported Doug Measures was unseated. In The Blue Mountains, CollingwoodToday reported Marni Moreau won with 2,469 votes, or 41.1 per cent, ahead of Paul Reale with 2,384 votes, or 39.7 per cent, and Peter Bordignon with 1,159 votes, or 19.3 per cent, with Rachel Gilliland as deputy mayor and councillors Brayden DeWitt, Meghan Loney, Shawn McKinlay, George McLeod and June Porter. CollingwoodToday said those Blue Mountains results are unofficial until the clerk certifies them, and that 6,147 of 15,154 eligible electors voted, a turnout of 40.6 per cent. Source: [bayshorebroadcasting.ca](https://www.bayshorebroadcasting.ca/2026/10/26/2026-municipal-election-results/) Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/2026-municipal-election-news/the-blue-mountains-election-results-12941604) Source: [ctvnews.ca](https://www.ctvnews.ca/barrie/video/2026/10/27/wasaga-beachs-election-results-heavily-delayed/) Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/local-news/doug-measures-unseated-in-clearview-as-mcarthur-wins-mayors-chair-12942217) Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/2026-municipal-election-news/collingwood-election-results-yvonne-hamlin-re-elected-12941592)

**Simcoe County public board enrolment down by more than 600 students: CollingwoodToday**
CollingwoodToday reports Simcoe County's public board enrolment is down by more than 600 students. The board notes more than 300 students registered late in September. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/local-news/simcoe-county-public-board-enrolment-down-by-more-than-600-students-12954801)

**Close Collingwood trustee race takes twists and turns: CollingwoodToday**
CollingwoodToday reports Julie Rose is the newly minted Collingwood/Wasaga Beach trustee after a close race. Rose said, "I'm very happy. I can't wait to get to work." Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/2026-municipal-election-news/close-collingwood-trustee-race-takes-twists-and-turns-12947307)

### Council & County
**Grey County Needs $28.7 Million More a Year to Keep Roads and Bridges in Good Shape: The Owen Sound Current**
The Owen Sound Current reports Grey County needs $28.7 million more a year to keep roads and bridges in good shape. CollingwoodToday reports the county is on track to close its infrastructure funding gap by 2038. Source: [owensoundcurrent.com](https://www.owensoundcurrent.com/p/grey-county-needs-287-million-more) Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/the-blue-mountains-and-grey-highlands/grey-county-on-track-to-close-infrastructure-funding-gap-by-2038-12939579)

### The Closer Look
**Grey County marketing campaign wins provincial award: CollingwoodToday**
Grey County's Gather in Grey campaign won the Tourism Industry Association of Ontario's Tourism Marketing Campaign Award in the over-$50,000 category. The award was presented at the 2026 Ontario Tourism Awards of Excellence in Ottawa on October 23, 2026. CollingwoodToday reported the win, and The Owen Sound Current reported the same award, category, date and city. CollingwoodToday said the award recognizes outstanding tourism marketing that inspires travel, builds destination awareness and helps grow Ontario's visitor economy.

Gather in Grey was selected from finalists including Explore Waterloo Region's brand launch campaign and Tourism Hamilton's Let Me Show You the Hamilton I Love campaign. It was also a finalist in the Tourism Digital Marketing Award category alongside Tourism Hamilton. Ottawa Tourism received that digital award for its Magic on Set campaign. Both outlets reported those finalist lists and that Ottawa Tourism took the digital prize.

The campaign was built with partner organizations. Funding came from the Province of Ontario through the Rural Ontario Development program and from Regional Tourism Organization 7 through its Partnership Fund. Roger Mooking, described by CollingwoodToday as an internationally recognized chef and artist, is Grey County's first creative director and culinary ambassador. The Owen Sound Current also described him as a television host. In a series of videos he travelled through Grey County meeting farmers, producers, restaurateurs, artisans, makers and tourism operators. CollingwoodToday said those videos showcased the region's creativity, entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community.

The campaign used video, photography, social media, digital and print advertising, connected television, radio, editorial content and trip-planning resources. Since the full launch in 2025, CollingwoodToday reported more than 50,000 trip idea views and 54,000 event page views. The Owen Sound Current reported 1.78 million impressions, more than 137,000 YouTube views and more than 315,000 website sessions.

Gather in Grey has grown from a campaign into the county's tourism brand and has replaced Visit Grey. Grey County now uses the name to guide destination marketing, including a new destination website. Savanna Myers, director of economic development, tourism and culture, said the recognition reflects tourism operators, businesses, artists, farmers, makers, community partners and residents whose stories continue to shape Grey County's tourism experience and its reputation as a destination where people come together. The Owen Sound Current reported that Myers credited tourism operators, businesses, farmers, artists and residents whose stories appear in the campaign. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/the-blue-mountains-and-grey-highlands/grey-county-marketing-campaign-wins-provincial-award-12952059) Source: [owensoundcurrent.com](https://www.owensoundcurrent.com/p/grey-countys-gather-in-grey-campaign)

### Also Today
**Georgian Bay General Hospital brings back stricter masking requirements: MidlandToday**
MidlandToday reports Georgian Bay General Hospital has brought back stricter masking, required during direct patient interactions because of rising respiratory illnesses. Source: [midlandtoday.ca](https://www.midlandtoday.ca/local-news/georgian-bay-general-hospital-brings-back-stricter-masking-requirements-12956469)

**Local residents call for retirement of York University's nine research monkeys: MidlandToday**
MidlandToday reports a Collingwood undercover investigator and a Tiny Township advocate are pressing for stronger protections and sanctuary retirement for nine research monkeys at York University. Source: [midlandtoday.ca](https://www.midlandtoday.ca/local-news/two-local-women-fight-for-future-of-yorks-nine-monkeys-12933441)

**10 tubing lanes, a mountaintop skating loop and a water park: Blue Mountain's winter is about more than skiing: Toronto.com**
Toronto.com reports Blue Mountain's winter includes 10 tubing lanes, a mountaintop skating loop and a water park, beyond skiing. Source: [toronto.com](https://www.toronto.com/news/blue-mountain-travel-ontario/article_81177db7-1a3e-51ae-85ef-a0635024160e.html)

**Grey County Launches Online Engagement Platform Connect Grey: The Meaford Independent**
The Meaford Independent reports Grey County has launched an online engagement platform called Connect Grey. Source: [themeafordindependent.ca](https://themeafordindependent.ca/grey-county-launches-online-engagement-platform-connect-grey/)

**Four Georgian Bay Titans head to U.K.: CollingwoodToday Sports**
CollingwoodToday Sports reports four Georgian Bay Titans are heading to the U.K., and the group aims to raise $8,000 to cover costs. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/local-sports/four-georgian-bay-titans-head-to-uk-12931808)

### Roads & Weather Ahead
Environment Canada says no watches or warnings are in effect for Collingwood. Friday is cloudy with a 40 percent chance of showers, a northwest wind of 30 km/h gusting to 50, a high of 9 and a UV index of 2 or low; the feed's current reading was 8.6°C. Friday night is mainly cloudy, with fog patches developing, a low of zero, and a northwest wind of 20 km/h gusting to 40 becoming light in the evening. Saturday is a mix of sun and cloud, with morning fog dissipating, a northwest wind of 20 km/h late in the morning, a high of 12 and a UV index of 3 or moderate; Saturday night is clear with a low of plus 2. Sunday is sunny with a high of 15. Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/44.5_-80.217_e.xml)

### The Weekend
**Photographer to present Niagara Escarpment book and talk in Collingwood: CollingwoodToday**
CollingwoodToday reports Mark Zelinski will be in Collingwood on November 5 for a free evening of photography, storytelling and stewardship tied to his book, Niagara Escarpment: Land Between Waters. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/local-news/photographer-to-present-niagara-escarpment-book-and-talk-in-collingwood-12939466)

**Simcoe County Museum to host virtual Remembrance Day lectures: MidlandToday**
MidlandToday reports the Simcoe County Museum will host free virtual Remembrance Day lectures on November 5 and November 26. Source: [midlandtoday.ca](https://www.midlandtoday.ca/local-news/simcoe-county-museum-to-host-virtual-remembrance-day-lectures-12940165)

# Collingwood Weekly
> **Collingwood CAO Sonya Skinner is one of two winners of Canada's public-service leadership award.**

**What You Need to Know:** Collingwood CAO Sonya Skinner is one of two winners of Canada's public-service leadership award, the 2026 Institute of Public Administration of Canada Established Leader Award, presented in Ottawa on October 7. A 33-year-old Wasaga Beach resident stands charged in a child exploitation investigation and is due in court on October 27. Grey County paramedic chief Kevin McNab is the only 2026 recipient of the Ontario Association of Paramedic Chiefs' Richard Armstrong Leadership Award.

### The Week's Stories
**Collingwood CAO Sonya Skinner Receives National Public Service Award: Barrie 360**
Collingwood chief administrative officer Sonya Skinner is one of two winners of the 2026 Institute of Public Administration of Canada Established Leader Award, which Barrie 360 describes as one of Canada's top public-service honours. The award was presented at IPAC's National Public Service Symposium in Ottawa on October 7, and Skinner was chosen from a national shortlist of seven. She has been Collingwood's CAO since 2020, after more than two decades in executive and board roles that included the Grey Sauble Conservation Authority and the Ontario Public Service, spanning municipal administration, environmental regulation, transportation, and information technology. Since joining the town she has led work on governance, financial sustainability, and community trust. Skinner said it is a great honour, that she is grateful, and that she is proud to work with dedicated colleagues and community leaders. Town officials said the award also reflects leadership across the organization, noting several municipal employees have been recognized this year. Source: [barrie360.com](https://barrie360.com/collingwood-cao-public-service-award/) Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/local-news/collingwoods-cao-gets-national-leadership-accolades-12920577)

**Wasaga Beach Resident Charged in Child Exploitation Investigation: Barrie 360**
The Ontario Provincial Police Child Sexual Exploitation Unit, with help from Peel Regional Police, executed a search warrant at a Wasaga Beach home on June 23 and seized several electronic devices. Police say the accused was arrested on September 12. The accused is charged with two counts of possession of child sexual abuse and exploitation material, one count of making that material, one count of accessing it, and one count of voyeurism. The accused is scheduled to appear in court on October 27. Source: [barrie360.com](https://barrie360.com/wasaga-beach-child-exploitation-investigation-charges/) Source: [ctvnews.ca](https://www.ctvnews.ca/barrie/article/opp-seize-devices-charge-wasaga-beach-resident-in-child-exploitation-investigation/)

**NVCA honours Lynn Dollin for nearly 20 years of source water work: CollingwoodToday**
The Nottawasaga Valley Conservation Authority has named the boardroom in the John Hix Administrative Centre the Lynn Dollin Boardroom. CollingwoodToday reports the naming recognizes nearly 20 years of leadership and service on the South Georgian Bay Lake Simcoe Source Protection Committee. BarrieToday identifies Dollin as the mayor of Innisfil. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/local-news/nvca-honours-lynn-dollin-for-nearly-20-years-of-source-water-work-12924167) Source: [barrietoday.com](https://www.barrietoday.com/local-news/dollin-honoured-by-nvca-for-remarkable-contribution-to-watershed-12923218)

### Council & County
**Reminder: Voting Period Open Until October 26: CollingwoodToday**
The Town of the Blue Mountains says the voting period remains open until October 26. The town has also shared key voting information ahead of the municipal election. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/town-of-blue-mountains/reminder-voting-period-open-until-october-26-12924915) Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/town-of-blue-mountains/town-shares-key-voting-information-ahead-of-municipal-election-12849491)

### The Closer Look
**Grey County Paramedic Chief earns provincial leadership award: CKNX News Today**
Grey County paramedic chief Kevin McNab is the sole recipient of the 2026 Richard Armstrong Leadership Award. The Ontario Association of Paramedic Chiefs presented it at the association's annual gathering in Niagara Falls earlier this month. Grey County council recognized him at its meeting on Thursday, October 22. The Owen Sound Current reports that the county says he was the only recipient this year. The award recognizes leadership, innovation, and contributions to paramedicine in Ontario.

McNab has worked for Grey County for more than 30 years, including nine years as paramedic chief. A county media release says he guided Grey County Paramedic Services toward a standout standard for community-based paramedicine, medical innovation, and seamless care delivery. He took the local Community Paramedicine Program from an initial trial to a service the county calls essential, one that aids hundreds of people managing chronic conditions. Community paramedics provide that care in patients' homes, outside emergency calls. He obtained provincial grants so the program could continue without adding costs for municipal taxpayers. He has also worked on paramedic training, Ontario-wide clinical guidelines, and health strategies the county credits with better patient care in Grey and across the province. During the COVID-19 pandemic, that leadership supported localized testing and vaccination outreach for high-risk residents. The Owen Sound Current says the service delivered in-home testing and vaccinations.

Grey County Warden Andrea Matrosovs said McNab's leadership has had a profound impact on healthcare in Grey County and beyond. She said he is never satisfied with the status quo and looks for new ways to improve care, support paramedics, and strengthen the healthcare system. She said his willingness to innovate, collaborate, and advocate has made Grey County a leader in community paramedicine, and that the county is proud of the provincial award. McNab said he is honoured and shares the recognition with the entire Grey County Paramedic Services team. He thanked county council for its support and leadership. He said the work is built on collaboration, dedication, and a shared commitment to the best possible care for residents. The county ties the honour to more than 160 paramedics and support personnel who care for the community every day, and says his career has developed emergency medical care and health outcomes for residents in Grey County and the wider region. Source: [cknxnewstoday.ca](https://cknxnewstoday.ca/midwestern/news/2026/10/23/grey-county-paramedic-chief-earns-provincial-leadership-award) Source: [owensoundsuntimes.com](https://www.owensoundsuntimes.com/news/grey-county-paramedic-chief-receives-provincial-award/) Source: [owensoundcurrent.com](https://www.owensoundcurrent.com/p/grey-county-paramedic-chief-kevin)

### Also Today

Grey County has backed a lower speed limit of 40 km/h for traffic through Feversham. Source: [owensoundsuntimes.com](https://www.owensoundsuntimes.com/news/grey-county-supports-lowering-speed-limit-to-40-km-h-through-feversham/)

Conditions were 4.0°C, with Friday mainly sunny after morning fog patches, a southeast wind of 20 km/h becoming light late in the morning, a high of 12, and a UV index of 3 or moderate. ### Sport
**'Incredibly special event': Young runners go the distance at Simcoe County championships: MidlandToday**
At Wednesday's Simcoe County elementary cross-country championships at Mount St. Louis Moonstone, Iris Matanowitsch of Nottawa Elementary School surged ahead to finish first, and Brianna Forrest of Minising Central Public School finished second. More than 1,800 student athletes competed. A Grade 5 student in the field told MidlandToday they were pretty excited and a bit nervous. # Collingwood Weekly
> **Collingwood council endorsed a 19-goal climate plan to steer budgets against heavier rain and heat.**

**What You Need to Know:** Collingwood council endorsed a 19-goal climate plan to steer budgets against heavier rain and heat. The plan now moves into work plans and ordinary budgets. Elsewhere this week, provincial police charged a Wasaga Beach resident in a March motel fire, and Blue Mountain set a December 10 opening day.

### The Week's Stories
**Collingwood endorses climate change adaptation plan: Ontario Construction News**
Council endorsed a Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan with 19 goals for heavier rainfall, flooding, extreme heat, shoreline erosion and warmer winters. The plan is organized around People and Community, Services and Operations, and Natural Environment, and is meant to guide planning and spending. Mayor Hamlin said in a statement, "Adaptation is about practical planning for weather conditions we are already seeing in Collingwood," and that preparing early protects residents, properties and services and can reduce emergency-repair costs. Local climate data, technical analysis, staff and regional partners, and community feedback shaped the risks and the measures. Endorsement moves the plan into implementation through work plans, budgets and asset management, with each investment still subject to the town's regular budget process. The plan also calls for stronger emergency planning and for information residents can use before extreme weather; the town encourages household emergency plans, clear drainage and eavestroughs, and checking on neighbours. Source: [ontarioconstructionnews.com](https://ontarioconstructionnews.com/collingwood-endorses-climate-change-adaptation-plan)

**Arson charge laid in Wasaga Beach motel fire: Barrie 360**
Ontario Provincial Police have charged a person in connection with a fire at the Villa Nova Motel on Mosley Street in Wasaga Beach. Crews responded shortly before midnight on March 9. Everyone inside evacuated safely, and no injuries were reported. This week police arrested a 58-year-old Wasaga Beach resident and charged them with arson, disregard for human life, and failing to comply with an undertaking. The accused has a court date on October 27. Source: [barrie360.com](https://barrie360.com/wasaga-beach-resident-charged-arson-motel-fire/) Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/police-beat/arson-charge-laid-in-wasaga-beach-motel-fire-12898981) Source: [barrietoday.com](https://www.barrietoday.com/police-beat/arson-charge-laid-in-wasaga-beach-motel-fire-12898981)

**ELECTION: Here's how many ballots have been cast in Collingwood so far: CollingwoodToday**
Collingwood's municipal election has 2,010 votes cast in the first week of internet voting. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/2026-municipal-election-news/election-heres-how-many-ballots-have-been-cast-in-collingwood-so-far-12895541)

**Blue Mountain Resort sets opening date for ski season: CKNX News Today**
Blue Mountain Resort will open the 2026-27 ski and snowboard season on Thursday, December 10, 2026, with activities starting at 8:30 a.m. The resort said, "Our teams are hard at work putting the finishing touches on the slopes, testing lifts, and preparing the mountain for your first turns of the season." This opening is one day later than last season, when the resort opened December 9 and ran until April 22. Blue Mountain, near Collingwood, is Ontario's largest ski and snowboard destination. The resort is telling visitors to check its website for trail conditions and hours as opening day approaches. Source: [cknxnewstoday.ca](https://cknxnewstoday.ca/news/2026/10/14/blue-mountain-resort-sets-opening-date-for-ski-season) Source: [ctvnews.ca](https://www.ctvnews.ca/barrie/article/blue-mountain-resort-unveils-opening-date-for-85th-winter-ski-season/)

**Notice of Construction: Wasaga Stars Arena & Wasaga Beach Public Library Parking Lot Expansion: Town of Wasaga Beach**
Tree clearing and earthworks for the Wasaga Stars Arena and Wasaga Beach Public Library parking-lot expansion started October 15, 2026, weather permitting, under contractor JB Enterprises. The Town of Wasaga Beach is providing contract administration and construction inspection. Residents should expect construction noise, equipment activity and truck traffic during permitted working hours. Questions go to Mike Pincivero, P.Eng., RMO/RMI, manager of engineering services. Source: [wasagabeach.com](https://www.wasagabeach.com/news/posts/notice-of-construction-wasaga-stars-arena-wasaga-beach-public-library-parking-lot-expansion/)

### Council & County
**Name a Grey County Snowplow: Submissions Open Until Oct. 22: The Owen Sound Current**
Grey County is taking snowplow names through October 22 at 11:59 p.m. on ConnectGrey.ca, and the contest is the first project on that new engagement site. Each person may submit up to three names. The county will publish top suggestions, public voting runs October 23 to November 6, and winning names will be announced November 10 for plows in each of four patrol areas. The four top entries win prize packs. Only entrants with a registered ConnectGrey account and an email are eligible for credit and prizes, and if more than one person submits the same name, only the first is eligible. Names must suit all ages; puns about winter, snow, plowing or the area are encouraged. Source: [owensoundcurrent.com](https://www.owensoundcurrent.com/p/name-a-grey-county-snowplow-submissions)

### The Closer Look
**Grey County, Owen Sound Face Uncertain Infrastructure Funding as Five-Year Boost Ends: The Owen Sound Current**
Grey County and Owen Sound received $7.5 million in 2026 from a provincial fund for roads, bridges and water systems whose five-year doubling expires this year. On October 8, Grey County's committee of the whole voted to support a June 25 letter from the Municipal Finance Officers' Association of Ontario to Acting Infrastructure Minister Todd McCarthy. The letter asks the province to make the doubled Ontario Community Infrastructure Fund permanent at $400 million a year before it calculates 2027 allocations. The province doubled the fund from about $200 million to $400 million a year beginning with 2022 allocations. The resolution notes no public commitment to keep that level beyond 2026.

Grey County received $1,279,946 in 2021, the last year before the doubling, $2,645,238 in 2022, and $3,836,916 in 2026. Owen Sound's allocation grew from about $1.1 million in 2021 to $3,647,845 in 2026. The county's deputy treasurer told the committee the fund is a fixed $400-million pool reweighted every year on the condition and replacement value of assets in each asset management plan. Grey County's larger share, the deputy treasurer said, has effectively come out of other municipalities' allocations, because the province has not increased the total over the five years. The province announced 2026 allocations in September 2025.

At the Association of Municipalities of Ontario conference in August, McCarthy was asked about continuing the doubled fund. He pointed to investments already made, including a new stream for municipalities that do not charge development charges, and did not commit to $400 million, according to a report from the Association of Municipal Managers, Clerks and Treasurers of Ontario. Coun. Eccles, who pulled the item from the consent agenda, argued $400 million falls well short once divided among eligible communities and said he wanted the fund raised every year to keep pace with costs. CAO Randy Scherzer said council has previously asked the province to account for inflation in municipal funding, and that an asset-management update due at the October 22 committee of the whole will include updated figures on Grey County's infrastructure needs. Coun. Greig said Buy Ontario rules, which now apply to municipalities, tend to raise prices by requiring domestic purchasing, which strengthens the case for more provincial funding. A September 15 letter from Municipal Affairs and Housing Minister Rob Flack, received for information without discussion, said failing to comply with Buy Ontario requirements "will force us to reconsider provincial funding made available to municipalities." Scherzer said staff will contact the Municipal Finance Officers' Association about its next steps. Source: [owensoundcurrent.com](https://www.owensoundcurrent.com/p/grey-county-owen-sound-face-uncertain)

### Roads & Weather Ahead
Environment Canada has no watches or warnings in effect for Collingwood. Friday is cloudy with a 60 percent chance of showers. Wind becomes northwest 20 km/h gusting to 40 late this morning, then 50 gusting to 70 late this afternoon. The high is 13, falling to 8 this afternoon, with a UV index of 2. Friday night stays cloudy, with a 60 percent chance of rain showers changing to a 60 percent chance of flurries after midnight, wind northwest 50 km/h gusting to 70 diminishing to 30 gusting to 50 late evening, and a low of minus 1. Saturday is a mix of sun and cloud with a 30 percent chance of flurries early, then sunny, wind north 20 km/h gusting to 40 becoming light late morning, and a high of 8. Saturday night is clear with a low of plus 4. Sunday is sunny with a high of 16. Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/44.5_-80.217_e.xml)

# Collingwood Weekly
> **Collingwood voters gained internet ballots at ten Thursday, ahead of October twenty-six.**

**What You Need to Know:** Collingwood voters gained internet ballots at ten Thursday, ahead of October twenty-six, and paper ballots are planned at more than one point through the rest of the month. Clearview’s window opens Monday, October 12, and runs to October 26, online, by phone, or at an Election Services Centre, using the voter information letters mailed in September. A Simcoe County Transit Service Delivery Review describes a split county-and-town network, Collingwood marked Probus Month for more than 2,300 residents in 10 local clubs, and the County of Simcoe says the Simcoe County Museum stays open Thanksgiving Monday while the archives close.

### The Week's Stories
**Voting starts today in Collingwood. Here's what you need to know: CollingwoodToday**
CollingwoodToday reports that internet voting in the town opened at 10 a.m. on October 8. The same account says multiple paper voting options are planned throughout the month, so a paper ballot is not limited to a single day. Election day is October 26. The opening of internet voting on October 8 is the dated start of the town’s voting period that runs to that election day. Paper options sit alongside the internet ballot for the remainder of the month. Residents who want a paper ballot have those planned options before October 26, and residents who want the internet ballot have had that route since 10 a.m. Thursday. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/2026-municipal-election-news/voting-starts-today-in-collingwood-heres-what-you-need-to-know-12856541)

**Councillors push for expanded transit links across Simcoe County: CollingwoodToday**
CollingwoodToday reports that councillors are pushing for expanded transit links across Simcoe County. The push follows a new Simcoe County Transit Service Delivery Review. That review says the region’s mix of county and municipal transit systems is fragmented. The review names three results of that split: gaps in coverage, separate fare structures, and inconsistent accessibility standards. Coverage gaps are the places the mixed systems do not reach as one network. Separate fare structures mean a rider can meet a different fare when the trip crosses from a county service to a municipal service, or the other way. Inconsistent accessibility standards mean the access rules are not the same from one of those systems to the next. The councillors’ push, as CollingwoodToday frames it, is for links that reach farther across the county than that fragmented mix now does. On October 2 this show was still on county roads and services as an open question; today’s new fact is the review’s finding of fragmentation, named with those three results, and the councillors’ push for wider links. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/local-news/councillors-push-for-expanded-transit-links-across-simcoe-county-12867312)

**Probus month marked with flag raising in Collingwood: CollingwoodToday**
Collingwood marked Probus Month with a flag raising, CollingwoodToday reports. More than 2,300 Collingwood-area residents are part of the 10 local clubs. The flag raising is the public mark of the month in town. The membership figure is the Collingwood-area total across those 10 clubs, not a count for a single club. The 10 clubs are the local set that holds that membership. The month being marked is Probus Month, and the place of the flag raising is Collingwood. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/local-news/probus-month-marked-with-flag-raising-in-collingwood-12872630)

### Council & County
**Clearview: Vote online, by phone or at an Election Services Centre Oct. 12 to 26: BarrieToday**
BarrieToday reports that Clearview electors can vote online, by phone, or at an Election Services Centre from October 12 to October 26. That is a 15-day window that starts Monday and ends on the same election day Collingwood uses, October 26. Voter information letters mailed in September have everything electors need to vote. Those letters include voting credentials. They include the voting website. They include the telephone number. They include the credentials needed to cast a vote. An elector using the internet uses the website and the credentials in that September letter. An elector using the phone uses the telephone number and the credentials in that letter. An elector who wants a staffed place uses an Election Services Centre inside the October 12 to 26 window. The three routes — online, phone, and an Election Services Centre — are all open across that same stretch of days. Source: [barrietoday.com](https://www.barrietoday.com/2026-municipal-election-news/clearview-vote-online-by-phone-or-at-an-election-services-centre-oct-12-to-26-12868041)

### Roads & Weather Ahead
Environment Canada has no watches or warnings in effect for Collingwood, and the current reading is 15.1 degrees. Friday is a mix of sun and cloud, wind northwest at 30 kilometres an hour gusting to 50, high 15, UV index 4 or moderate. Friday night is clear, becoming partly cloudy after midnight, with a low of plus 4. Saturday is sunny, the wind becoming southeast at 20 kilometres an hour late in the morning, high 18, UV index 4 or moderate, and Saturday night brings cloudy periods with a low of 10. Sunday is cloudy with a 30 percent chance of rain and a high of 19. Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/44.5_-80.217_e.xml)

### The Weekend
**Simcoe County Museum to open Thanksgiving Monday while archives close: BarrieToday**
BarrieToday reports that the County of Simcoe is advising residents of service and facility schedule changes for Thanksgiving Day on Monday. The Simcoe County Museum will be open that Monday. The archives will be closed that Monday. The county’s advice covers service changes and facility schedule changes for the holiday, and the museum-open, archives-closed split is the change the report names. Thanksgiving Day this year falls on Monday, and that Monday is the day the museum stays open while the archives do not. Source: [barrietoday.com](https://www.barrietoday.com/local-news/simcoe-county-museum-to-open-thanksgiving-monday-while-archives-close-12870029)

# Collingwood Weekly
> **Wasaga council approved 214 Beachwood Road homes after a flood-channel land promise.**

**What You Need to Know:** Wasaga Beach council approved amendments for a 214-unit project on Beachwood Road after a flooding reassurance, with a large petition and environmental concerns still on the record. Collingwood had a house fire that forced three adults out, and impaired-driving charges followed local crashes. A $2-billion Wasaga beach-and-downtown vision is on the table, mayor and deputy mayor candidates met on transportation, and the weekend forecast turns clearer after Friday’s wind.

### The Week's Stories
**Three adults evacuated after a Collingwood house fire: CTV News**
Fire officials told CTV News that three adults had to be evacuated after a house fire in Collingwood on Wednesday. Officials said there was extensive damage to the home. Source: [ctvnews.ca](https://www.ctvnews.ca/barrie/video/2026/10/01/three-adults-had-to-be-evacuated-after-a-house-fire-in-collingwood-wednesday/)

**Impaired charges after Collingwood-area crashes: CollingwoodToday**
CollingwoodToday reports that two crashes in one day left a Collingwood resident and an Elmvale resident facing impaired charges, with licences suspended and charges to be faced in court. BarrieToday reports that officers were called Monday evening to a collision at Hume Street and Highway 26 in Collingwood, and that an Elmvale resident was charged with impaired driving. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/police-beat/two-crashes-in-one-day-leave-two-drivers-with-impaired-charges-12845564) Source: [barrietoday.com](https://www.barrietoday.com/police-beat/elmvale-resident-charged-with-impaired-driving-after-crash-opp-12845741)

**Wasaga destination plan sets out a $2-billion vision: Simcoe.com**
Simcoe.com reports that a Wasaga Beach destination plan sets out a $2-billion vision for the main beach and downtown. Source: [simcoe.com](https://www.simcoe.com/news/council/wasaga-beach-destination-downtown-beachfront/article_b8a6bf82-e736-5391-ae50-e61424ff0977.html)

**Garage containing boats burns in Georgian Bay: CTV News**
CTV News reports that a garage containing boats in Georgian Bay went up in flames. Source: [ctvnews.ca](https://www.ctvnews.ca/barrie/article/garage-containing-boats-in-georgian-bay-goes-up-in-flames/)

**Jane Peck named an Unsung Hero: CollingwoodToday**
CollingwoodToday’s Community Builders Awards recognize Jane Peck as an Unsung Hero for years of service to local youth and the wider community. The recognition is tied to the Head Strong Initiative, described as helping youth take the next step toward better mental health. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/cbawards/winners/the-head-strong-initiative-is-helping-youth-take-the-next-step-to-better-mental-health-12769579)

### Council & County
**Mayor and deputy mayor candidates talk transportation: CollingwoodToday**
The Collingwood Chamber of Commerce organized an all-candidates meeting at the Collingwood legion on Sept. 30. Mayor and deputy mayor candidates talked transportation. Jon Hillis, Yvonne Hamlin, Chris Potts, Norman Sandberg, Kathy Jeffery and Deb Doherty attended. CollingwoodToday also reports that 19 people are running for seven Collingwood council seats in the fall municipal election. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/2026-municipal-election-news/mayor-deputy-mayor-candidates-talk-transportation-at-legion-12844129) Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/2026-municipal-election-news/election-heres-where-collingwood-councillor-candidates-stand-on-development-12809154)

**New integrity commissioner starts December 1: The Owen Sound Current**
The Owen Sound Current reports that a new integrity commissioner for Owen Sound and Grey County starts December 1. Source: [owensoundcurrent.com](https://www.owensoundcurrent.com/p/new-integrity-commissioner-for-owen)

**School board seeks special-education advisory representatives: MidlandToday**
The Simcoe County District School Board is inviting local agencies, associations and organizations to nominate representatives to its Special Education Advisory Committee. Source: [midlandtoday.ca](https://www.midlandtoday.ca/local-news/school-board-seeks-community-representatives-for-special-education-advisory-committee-12840991)

### Roads & Weather Ahead
No watches or warnings are in effect for Collingwood, and Environment Canada listed current conditions at 11.0°C. Friday’s showers end early this morning, then it clears, with a northwest wind of 30 km/h gusting to 50, a high of 17 and a UV index of 5, or moderate. Friday night brings a few clouds and fog patches, a northwest wind of 20 km/h gusting to 40 becoming light this evening, and a low of plus 5. Saturday is mainly sunny once morning fog patches dissipate, with a high of 18 and a UV index of 4, or moderate, then a clear night and a low of 9. Sunday is a mix of sun and cloud with a 30 percent chance of showers and a high of 17. Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/44.5_-80.217_e.xml)

### The Weekend
**Rodeo returns to Wasaga Beach: Simcoe.com**
Simcoe.com points to a rodeo returning to Wasaga Beach this weekend, and to free pumpkin painting in Barrie. Source: [simcoe.com](https://www.simcoe.com/things-to-do/three-events-simcoe-county/article_f3189742-fa64-50d3-8b9d-0ad2f6fd0388.html)

### Both Sides: Wasaga Beachwood Road housing
Wasaga Beach council approved amendments for a housing project on Beachwood Road after reassurance that flooding issues will be resolved. Simcoe.com reports the project is for 214 units. The developer will give land to the town for a channel to mitigate flooding. Staff found the project consistent with planning policies. The strongest case for the amendments is that staff finding: the project fits the planning policies already in place, and the land for a channel is the step offered to deal with flooding.

Residents raised concerns about environmental degradation, and a conservation authority raised concerns about environmental degradation as well. Nearly 2,800 people signed a petition against the plan. Some councillors had previously signed a petition opposing the project. The strongest case against it is that environmental concern, made by residents and by the conservation authority, alongside a petition of nearly 2,800 people and the fact that some councillors had themselves signed on against the plan.

The fact sitting with both arguments is the Beachwood Road project itself: 214 units, a staff finding that it is consistent with planning policies, and a petition against it that drew nearly 2,800 signatures. Council approved the amendments after reassurance that flooding issues will be resolved. The developer will give the town land for a channel to mitigate flooding. Source: [simcoe.com](https://www.simcoe.com/news/council/wasaga-beach-romanin-flooding/article_bc6c2a1d-a96d-5ce5-8d25-da8263e0ea54.html)

# Collingwood Weekly
> **Police captured a bull moose in Collingwood and will move him north.**

**What You Need to Know:** On Tuesday, police, firefighters and provincial staff tranquilized a young bull moose at Collingwood’s waterfront and loaded him for a move farther north. Simcoe County is planning a one-day controlled burn on about 5 hectares in the Nottawasaga Tract in Clearview, as early as late September. Highway 26 has nightly full closures in Clearview, and no weather warnings are in effect.

### What This Show Covers
Every Friday morning, the week in Collingwood and the south Georgian Bay towns — Wasaga Beach, Clearview and The Blue Mountains — is gathered for year-round residents, weekenders, seasonal workers, business owners and parents who want to know what the town, the county and the bay did, and what the weekend holds. That means council and county decisions on budget, development, water, roads and services; the local economy when a number is attached; public safety from a named police or fire source; local sport results; and events a source names with a date and a place. Roads and weather come only from Ontario 511 and Environment Canada. When a local issue is contested, each side is given in its strongest form, best reason first, attributed by name, so a listener cannot tell which side the show prefers.

The round-up is read by Mira, the network's AI host. She says so. She does not claim to live here, to have skied the hill, walked the harbour or attended a meeting. She speaks as a well-informed host who read the week's local news so you do not have to. The stories are chosen and written by software from named local newsrooms and public data, and every item names its source. The one thing it will not do is speculate about people — no guesses about anyone's motives, guilt, health or private life.

Collingwood Weekly is part of the Nerra Network, an independent network of shows at nerranetwork.com. You are welcome to look around if another show would be useful to someone you know.

### The Week's Stories
**Bull moose tranquilized in Collingwood, taken away in trailer:** BarrieToday
After about three days of sightings reported to Collingwood and The Blue Mountains OPP, a young bull moose was located Tuesday morning in Harbourview Park and tranquilized by Bear Wise staff in the Arboretum at about noon. He ran into the water by the bridge at Harbourview Park, east of the Awen Gathering Circle, and collapsed from the dart. Bear Wise staff and OPP went into the water to pull him to shore; Collingwood firefighters and more officers, including detachment commander Insp. Loris Licharson, then loaded him on a plastic sled and used a winch to pull him up the bank into a trailer. Police nicknamed him Elliot. Bear Wise staff, who came from Midhurst, will take him farther north. Naturalist David Hawke, on scene with CollingwoodToday, confirmed it was a bull moose and said he had also been spotted in Thornbury the day before. Source: [barrietoday.com](https://www.barrietoday.com/local-news/bull-moose-tranquilized-in-collingwood-taken-away-in-trailer-12808515)

**County of Simcoe to conduct controlled burn in Clearview:** County of Simcoe
The County of Simcoe will conduct a controlled burn on about 5 hectares, or 12.5 acres, in the County Forest Nottawasaga Tract at 793455 County Road 124 in Clearview. It may start as early as conditions allow in late September or early October, is expected to take one day, and was delayed from spring 2026 by weather. The county says the burn responds to debris and brush left after salvage of trees damaged in the 2025 ice storm, so the site can be reached for reforestation; the property will be replanted and stay part of the county’s 34,000 acres of municipal forest. Lands and Forests Consulting is contracted to run the burn. Smoke is to disperse to the northeast, east or southeast, and possibly into the next day; the county says it does not anticipate road closures. Residents with asthma or chronic lung disease who live near the burn may wish to stay indoors, and anyone with health concerns should follow their health care provider. Source: [simcoe.ca](https://simcoe.ca/featured-news/county-of-simcoe-to-conduct-controlled-burn-in-clearview-2/)

**Collingwood man arrested for armed robbery of a Circle K:** CollingwoodToday
A 32-year-old Collingwood man was arrested on September 20. He is charged in connection with an armed robbery of a Circle K in Collingwood. Source: [collingwoodtoday.ca](https://www.collingwoodtoday.ca/police-beat/collingwood-man-arrested-for-armed-robbery-of-a-circle-k-12807033)

### Council & County
**Nomination deadline extended for 14th Annual Newcomer Recognition Awards:** County of Simcoe
The County of Simcoe has extended the nomination deadline for the 14th Annual Newcomer Recognition Awards to Friday, September 25, 2026. Community members may nominate individuals, organizations and businesses for contributions to the lives of newcomers in Simcoe County. The Simcoe County Local Immigration Partnership has hosted the event for the past 13 years; Honda Canada Mfg. is the gold sponsor. Nominations are at simcoe.ca/newcomer-recognition-awards. Source: [simcoe.ca](https://simcoe.ca/advisory/nomination-deadline-extended-for-14th-annual-newcomer-recognition-awards/)

### Roads & Weather Ahead
Nightly construction is closing all lanes of Highway 26 westbound in Clearview between Locke Avenue and Mosley Street at Simcoe Road 92, and all lanes eastbound on the same stretch. Highway 26 eastbound also has a daily moving maintenance closure, with one alternating lane, between Poplar Sideroad in Clearview and Carson Road in Springwater, and a nightly moving closure with one alternating lane between Lakeview Avenue in Clearview and Carson Road. No watches or warnings are in effect for Collingwood. Wednesday is mainly sunny, with an east wind of 20 km/h gusting to 40 and a high of 17; Wednesday night is clear with a low of 7. Thursday is sunny with a high of 19, and Thursday night is clear with a low of 6. Source: [511on.ca](https://511on.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/44.5_-80.217_e.xml)
